sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hey, how you doing?
Yeah, I'm very well, Andy.
How are you?
Yeah, I'm good, thank you.
Is it in Ncube and Ncube?
Yeah, it is.
Or Shep, which do you prefer?
Yeah, Shep is good.
How you doing?
Yeah, I'm very well, thank you.
Whereabouts are you based, Shep?
I'm based in the Isle of Man.
In the Isle of Man.
Oh, wow.
How long have you been there?
Sorry?
How long have you been there?
I've just been here for a few months.
Came in April, so.
Yeah, just.
Just a few months now.
Oh, really?
Are you a tax exile or.
How can you.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Texas.
Yeah.
Really?
Yeah.
Do you normally live in the UK or somewhere?
Yeah, normally.
Well, I'm from Zimbabwe, but I've been in the UK for 20 years, so I lived in Borden the last 12 or so years.
Brilliant.
In Altrim.
Yeah, in Altrim.
I see.
Okay, cool.
Yeah, we.
We had an agency actually listed.
Listed in the Isle of Man for sale.
Maybe it's something we can talk about in a bit.
I can introduce you to them or.
Well, so look, first of all, thank you for your patience and apologies for all of the problems that seem to have been going on with Deal Engines.
I can give you a little bit of background about that as well.
But really I'd just like to, if possible, reset our relationship.
I wasn't aware actually that you were an agency buyer.
I could see that you'd.
He'd been a subscriber on the Deal Engines platform.
But Deal Engines was an experimental thing for us.
We actually acquired a very small agency in January which was called Marketing Engines and we rebranded it Deal Engines.
But the actual processes weren't there and the delivery wasn't there.
So ultimately we decided to pull away from the business and the founder so that we could run the systems that we normally run for our clients as a M and A advisory.
So we're Capital A.
Capital A is an M and A advisory for marketing services businesses.
So we work both buying the sell side, either with marketing agency owners helping them to sell their business.
So we have the Platform agencies co, which is a marketplace for buyers and sellers.

We work on the buy side as well, either with sort of ambitious agency owners that are looking to roll other businesses into their agency or form a group, or we work with private equity or private investors helping them to find targets, either a platform business or bolt ons and tuck ins, working with them to help them grow and exit their investments as well.
So that's our usual business.
I'D love to hear a little bit more about what it is that you do.
And Ncube, so that we can understand what it is that you, you were trying to achieve through the Deal Engines platform.
Yeah, yeah.
So be good to know, are you actually an agency owner or are you just invested in?
Yeah, I mean, I'll sort of like give you a background.
I'm not an agent owner, but when I spoke with Daniel, I did tell him I'm looking to do some deals.
I've got a property marketing business.
I call it a property marketing because essentially that's what we, we generate about 6,000 leads a month through paid advertising and a little bit of SEO.
And obviously one of the things I've always been doing for the last 10, 15 years is marketing, whether from newspapers, transitioning into Facebook, Google, Adwords.
And I've got a small team, we've got a budget of 200,000.
But naturally I've always liked the market inside.
So I want to exit my business, which is Springboard Properties.
So I'm looking to sell that in the next, as soon as I can, basically.
And I'm hoping to get a marketing business as a platform and build on that.
But also while I'm doing marketing as well, I'll be looking at other opportunities to buy businesses.
Shep to me is something where I'm sort of like, say if I exit that, I'll have my family secure and then from there almost like play the game of business.
Basically, that's what I want to do, but I think central to what I'm doing.
I want marketing to be central of whatever I do because I do enjoy that aspect.
But I also believe, you know, the world is led by marketing, you know, in lead generation.
And I think, you know, if, if I've got that part, I think I will be able to acquire more businesses in future, in other verticals as well.

And I want marketing and sort of like the central of what I do, not necessarily just for short term to buy and flip, but to keep long terms as almost like my central office and you know, where I start off a lot of things.
Yeah, yeah, no, that's a, it's a, it's a common approach actually.
We worked with that.
And the other thing that I'm, I'm sort of like exploring that I've been thinking about because I see this challenge with us.
We, we don't know where we will end up with AI.
Obviously nowadays I, my searches are as much on chat AI platforms as.
Yeah.
So I'm, I'm Worried about that side of things.
And I thought, okay, if I do obtain an agency, one of the things I'll be adding on is AI so that, you know, we can help businesses that are already the client base to edge on AI.
So that, those are things that I've been thinking.
Yeah, okay.
And so just to sort of get a bit of clarity about that.
So Shep Properties is a, an investment.
Is that your investment company?
You invest in properties and you've got.
A. Yeah, we buy.
We buy and sell.
So it's a running company.
It's a trading company.
I've got about 105 employees, 87 in the UK and then, you know, I've got some people in India, Dubai, Philippines, South Africa, but the majority 80% are in the UK are in Manchester.
And yeah, we've got, yeah, they say EBITDA probably 5 million.
Last year, EBITDA was 5 million as well.
So it's a, it's a good, profitable business.
But I feel it's time to exit that so that, you know, I sort of like, secure my family and, you know, I can.
Okay.
So it's kind of like an investment stroke estate agency where you're, you're looking for properties to buy, but you, you're, you're bringing them in yourself and then flipping.
Yeah, we, we do both.
We buy and sell, but we also sell on behalf of clients, so we do both.
Wow, what a business.
Sounds phenomenal.
Congratulations.
That's amazing.
Good for me.
It's been good for me, to be honest.
Yeah, yeah, brilliant.
Okay, cool.
And then the, the marketing business that you have, what's that called?
If I can get an idea of what it is that you're doing with that.
No, no, I don't have a marketing business.
So the employees, where we market, generally it's our employed within Shep, I find I end up spending a lot of time with them.
And I've always thought, oh, a marketing business is a natural progression for me to buy the next thing.
Because obviously we, unlike most businesses with property, every month we have to get new leads.
So we get 6,000 leads every month.
So I feel by default.
I've studied, you know, funnels, landing pages, paid ads.
I don't know how a marketing agency runs.
That's the honest truth.
But I know employees, I know building teams, and I know marketing.
So I just thought it's a natural fit for me.
So.
Yeah, okay, I understand.
And I also like the, the aspect of recurring income.
So any business that I go into, I should have recurring income.
Okay, cool.
And whereabouts are you in the process of selling Shep?
If you put that up in the market, if you're going through that process.
So they prepare the IM and everything else.
Unfortunately, we uncovered some mistakes from my previous accountants.
I've moved accountants.
We are now on the audit threshold.
We're meant to be audited, but we're not.
So the new accountants are just doing the audit files.
And there were some issues around VAT and a couple of other issues that are being sorted.
So I'm hoping I'll put it on the market in October again.
Okay.
But we, we, we hadn't yet, but everything was almost ready.
But then we uncovered a few issues with the accounting side.
Yeah, cool.
And where are you selling that?
Just out of interest, are you, are you going with a broker or one of the big sites?
Yeah, I work with the broker, but every, the few people that I've spoken with, they'll say that made a mistake with a broker that I chose.
So I went with KBS and everyone was like, oh no, you shouldn't have gone with kbs.
And you know.
Yeah, I think, I mean we're specialists in, in the, in our market.
So I think always going with a specialist is probably better than one of big general generalist.
But yeah.
Okay, so, so you, you, you understand the marketing industry because you're basically marketing the, the opportunities that you have within Shep to get buyers on board.
So I get that's the direction you want to go and in terms of what it is you're looking for.
So are you looking to acquire just in the uk?
What, what's the deal with that?
So I mean, I'll speak with you frankly in terms of what my goals are in terms of.
Obviously I've moved to the Isle of Man.
I could like part of my life to be Isle of Man and usa.
I've always believed, you know, USA has a big potential for, for me as a, for my own personal growth.
So if it's the uk, that's fine.
If it's us, I mean, preferable.
Now I'll prepare you UK because I'm more familiar.
But I want to have a foothold in the usa.
So I'm just saying this to you so that you know, I'm.
I know.
I think you do business in USA as well.
So I don't.
We're probably about 90, 95% of our business is US based.
So.
Okay.
And why.
Yeah, well, so, so during COVID basically I built a business before in, in the US and when Covid hit.
I'd been, I'd been as an M and a advisor, going to everybody's offices, you know, all over London.
And as soon as lockdown happened I just knew the, the US well and that the market there is like 10 times bigger.
So we, we couldn't physically be anywhere so we might as well just be in the USA as well.
And we, we just started targeting buyers and sellers in the US and it just grew pretty naturally from that.
There are also a lot of buyers in the US looking for UK and European businesses anyway, so there was always a little bit of that.
But yeah, we just took the opportunity by both hands and grew into the us so the majority of work we do now is US buyers or sellers.
So we have more.
And you find that easier to deal with.
Less skeptical than the UK ones, isn't it?
Yeah, more ambitious, they've got more money, more money to invest.
Tax rules are better there as well.
So yeah, just, just there is more, more of everything there.
Particularly the attitude around buying is better.

What we see in the UK is, I mean there's still a buoyant market in the uk, particularly around marketing agencies, but you tend to get a lot more, you know, the buyers are looking for really low cost everything, so low multiples, you know.
So if we're working with a seller, if we sell to a UK company, it's likely it's going to be very low single digit multiples.
Whereas in the US we can get much, much higher, you know, single digit or even double digits as well.
So, so just is.
But it's a better seller's market.
But we do work with UK buyers as well, so.
And there's plenty of businesses in the uk, they just tend to be smaller, I think.
So it really does depend on what the investment is that you're looking for and what your strategy is.
So, so my thoughts about being my next progress, say are good based on what you're saying as well.
Yeah, yeah.
Okay.
So I mean what we could do if we were, if we were looking on your behalf, we, we would just spread it across uk, US and Isle of Man.
All right, let's have a look at what else you look for in terms of size.
Is there a size agency and is there a type of agency that you're looking for?
Yeah.
So when I spoke with Daniel, I did say I'm not sure yet, but obviously what I know from my experience is much better if it's bigger.
But again that will depend on how much, how will I finance it?
You know, that that that's because I always believe bigger is better in terms of management and the structures are already in place.
Yeah, yeah.
So like I would say a stable agency, when we're working on the buyer side, we tend to be asked to look for agencies that are above 10 people, including, not including the founders.
So agencies that are sort of 11, 12 people and bigger are slightly more stable.
Most marketing agencies are really founder focused, so the founder is usually still involved in the day to day.
Even if the business is up to about 3 to 5 million in revenue, they still tend to have founders involved.
And then beyond that, once the businesses get up between 5 and 10 million revenue, then the founder tends to step back from the day to day is more focused on building the business.
So that's what we tend to see.
And then in terms of ebitda, because the multiples are always on ebitda, you said you're not really sure about how to fund it, but I guess it would be some equity.
Sorry, some capital from you.
Yeah, Cash from my side.
Yeah, yeah.
And then debt.
And the US has got some, some brilliant things there.
They've got an SBA loan system.
I don't know if you've heard of that.
Yeah, I've heard of it, but I, I didn't think it applied to people like the British citizen like myself.
Yeah, it, it doesn't directly, no.
I think there are ways around it, but certainly if you got residency there, it would change.
If you had a business based there, you, you would be a, you'd be able to get an SBA loan.
They tend to be up to about 5 million for small businesses and they're backed by the government.
I think 80% is backed by the government.

And if you helped UK entrepreneurs transition into, I suppose yourself, you have transitioned into sort of like US holdings and everything else needed to be, to be able to access US loans, like SBA loans.
Is that possible for someone like myself?
We wouldn't be involved in that directly.
We do refer people.
I would say until you've got some kind of residency in the us then it would be difficult to get them.
They are for U.S. residents with U.S. businesses.
So those, I think those are the two qualifiers.
So as long as you were there on, on some kind of, you know, one visa, if you had a visa, a current visa, and you were running a business in the us, I think they're available to you.
So it might be too early, but definitely worth looking at.
Okay, so.
So just sort of, generally speaking in size, I should imagine if you were going to put, I don't know, a certain percentage into the deal you'd be looking for what, what is a maximum valuation?
Something like 5 million.
So a 5, a 5x on 1 million EBITDA.
Would that be where you're looking or smaller than that?
What type of financing would I get in terms of marketing agencies?
Do you know?
Sorry, I wouldn't know.
No, but it tends to be some, somewhere around 20 to 30% of your own capital for business loans.
So I guess similar to mortgages the way they are.
Yeah, so yeah, yeah.
So probably something like 5 million yen.
Yeah.
Okay, five minutes.
Do you, with the deals, do you structure announce or.
It's normally 80% cash or what's the normal structure that you get?
Yeah, so normally the way that deals are structured, I mean every deal is different and SBA loans are actually completely different.
But usually when we have an established business acquiring an agency, they are structured with 50% cash upfront and a three year earn out.
So you would pay the rest of the 50% due over the next three years.
And the idea is because the founder is so heavily involved that it takes kind of that long for them to untangle from the business.
So the sort of larger deals, they tend to have that kind of structure where it's 50% cash up front, three year earner.
And so the founder then is motivated to hit financial targets as they exit the business.
And then obviously you would, you would bring in somebody new to run the business during that, that process as well.
So the final year you might bring in a CEO to, to ghost them.
So yeah, I mean that's kind of the standard, but the, every, every kind of variation is there in the market.
Some, some sellers want to get out quicker, 6 months, 12 months to get out.
But obviously you would adjust the pric risk of somebody getting out of the business quickly.

So if, if a 1 million EBITDA business usually gets around a 5x multiple, but the founder wanted to get out in 12 months, for instance, you might want to look for a four and a half or a four times multiple on the ebitda.
That's how it generally works.
Okay.
So we've got a couple of ways that we can continue to work together.
Obviously we can, we, we actually work on the buy side, but it's, it's a, I mean it's not a SaaS business.
It's you know, a white glove business where we're working on your account on a daily basis.
So we could certainly do that.
Obviously you are now in the Market for an agency.
So the first thing we would want to do is put you on our mailing list of Agencies co.

I don't know if you've actually ever looked at agencies, whether Daniel even referred you to it, but we have a website, Agencies Co. We've got a portfolio of, of agencies for sale there, so it might be a good start to have a look at that.
I've just dropped it in the chat, so if you can click the link that will take you straight into the listings part of the site.
So we do have agencies already listed there.
I think there's, there's a couple of UK businesses in there, but it's mostly us.
Okay, okay.
I mean it's various.
We got stuff in Switzerland, Hong Kong, Turkey, Israel.
There's.
It is a global listing site.
Yeah, okay.
So, so yeah, let's, let's have a look at those that are already listed live.
But, but again, obviously you've come to us for us to generate those deals for you.
Generate the deal flow.
Is that something that is in of interest to you or are you just looking to do the deal flow yourself with your team?
No, no, no, it's of interest to me because I don't know where to start.
And do you have.
Obviously I don't have experience, so I don't know what, what I don't know, you know, in terms of what's the right business.
And yeah, I, I think the first acquisition, very important.
What's the journey for people that have never been agents or owners like myself?
Yeah, so.
So we've worked with, with multiple people in your situation where they're kind of coming from an investor approach and looking to build up a portfolio of agency businesses.
For instance, we work in, we're still working with a company called Skyview.
Actually we acquired two agencies for them last year.
One was in Denver and one was in the UK in London.
And they've merged those two businesses and we're now acquiring their third and fourth business.
And they had no experience at all of agencies.
They actually came from a cloud computing background, very experienced in investing and growing businesses, but not the actual agency part of it.
So my team are agency.
Usually they're senior members of agencies themselves as well as myself.
I bought and sold my own media and marketing business which I sold in 2016.
So we bring our experience to the table and also with agency owners, they tend to be fairly creative or they're quite immersed in the agency world.
So we bring that sort of knowledge and know how to the table.
And if you're not experienced as an agency buyer.
It brings credibility as well that we understand the space.
Like particularly with Skyview, the sellers were quite skeptical to sell to somebody with no experience.
But we actually had in the U.S. i've got a, an associate called Heather Fullerton and she's an ex managing director of a very large agency in New York.
So she was able to bring a deal in basically because people could see who she was and what her experience was.

So yeah, we're definitely used to working with investors that don't have agency experience and part of that know how as well is, is looking into the, the right types of agencies that you're trying to acquire.
And so we, I mean we are there every step of the way.
We're in every meeting.
We, we work with you all the way through due diligence, working on the request for information, etc.
So we're.
The only thing we don't offer is financial or legal advice.
Those, those would have to come from somewhere else.
But we do absolutely everything else, start to finish to get the deal closed.
Yeah.
Okay.
Okay, cool.
So, so the way that we work is it's a monthly retainer.
So it's 4,000 pound retainer and we have a 1.5% win fee on that as well.
So as soon as we get a deal closed then we're, we're due for, for the, the win fee as well.
So.
But like I said we, we usually have structured deals where it's 50 up front and we actually take our, our win fees at the same rate that you're paying out the seller as well.
I can stick that in a, in a email for you so you've got it in front of you and either we, we can roll the, the 500 pounds that we owe you or refund it one or the other.
I'm happy to do either because I can see that you haven't got much value out of deal engines.
Well, it just means all the thing basically but you know, it's one of those things.
Okay.
So what I will say at the moment is I've got a couple of focuses in my thing obvious to launch my business for sale.
I will probably say I will be ready in January.
But what I would like to do is to be to me everything I do.
I almost look at it like shopping when I go to a new shop.
I'm not always.
It's just the same with houses and if you start looking for a house in a new area, you're not aware you don't quite know the Price.
But I feel if I'm part of, I'm looking at the stuff that you're putting out on agency call, I'll start being familiar and by January I believe I'll be ready.
I want to put my, my business up for sale first, get some traction into that.
And yeah, I've just come here.
I will also be getting dividends from my business now, so I will.
I'm stacking up a little bit of cash as well and obviously look at financing as well.
So I'll be doing that.
I've already subscribed for.
I don't know what it's called, but you know the tax number in usa.
So what I'll do is also look for lawyers so that I'm open for both US and UK markets.
So by January I should be ready for all those things.
Yeah.
Okay, brilliant.
And into just in terms of the debt that you raise as well.
So we do work alongside some private debt providers.
So we, we work with one in the UK and the US So I'm happy to give you a referral to them.
They might be more suitable than like a high street bank because they kind of invest along alongside you.
I'm not 100 sure what their minimum deal size is, but they would definitely be able to.

Yeah, but, but I think it's much better knowing than I know I'm backing on the right tree and if, if I'm short somewhere I sort of like try and meet those things before, before January so that by January I'm ready to go.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
All right, so I'll send you some more information on email with some case studies as well and then I'll put a reminder in my calendar to, to catch up with you mid January.
And do you have any recommendation for me to educate myself?
Agents, owner, agency buyer and agency business builder.
Do you have any books, podcasts I can be listening to or anything that you think will be suitable courses for.
Yeah, so I can say I can send you my podcast.
So we've got podcasts with agency acquirers.
So people have been either been through the process of selling or acquiring themselves.
So there's plenty of podcasts to listen to there, including one with Martin Sorrel, who's one of the biggest agency acquirers in the world.
He's the founder of wpp, which is the largest marketing agency in the world.
I also have a agency acquirers course as well.
Okay, so I can send you that.
It's pretty cheap right now.
I think it's about £150 or something, it's fairly cheap.
Again, we can probably, we can take that off the money that we owe you and I can stick you in there for free.
Yeah, so yeah, let's do that then.
Yeah, that'll be fair.
Yeah.
All right, I'll sign you up to that.
And then there's like, I think there's about 15 videos to watch.
They're usually about 20, 30 minutes long.
Okay.
And they just go through the whole process of how we're doing it.
And, and what do you think of the agency market generally from somebody that's bought, sold and doing a lot of deals?
What do you think it looks like in the threads of AI as well?
To the, to the, to that industry?
Yeah, so there are, there are definitely specific agency types where the threat of AI is, is pretty bad.
You know, they're going to change the landscape drastically.
But there are other businesses that are probably going to be around for a long time regardless.
So certainly what we've seen in the market is influencer agency being, being really valuable and holding their value over time.
And there's a couple of other types.
You know, I'll send you a blog post that explains the different agency types and the value for them.
But yeah, there is like content.

We've got a client that works as a content agency for E commerce businesses and they provide all of the images that go on E commerce and they're obviously, you know, they've got a big expensive studio in New York and for them they've got massive high overheads.
There's probably some kid in his bedroom churning out thousands of photographs using AI for you know, a fraction of the price.
So those types of businesses are definitely.
Yeah, but, but again, another thing that we see that's really valuable and this is your space is the lead gen agencies.
Lead gen agencies are super popular.
Everybody wants to buy one.
As soon as we list a lead gen agency, we've got lots of interest instantly.
So those are, those are definitely the ones to look for, I think.
Okay.
Okay.
Yeah, probably that's what I will specialize in because I've been looking at lead gen agencies a lot because again, you own the system, isn't it?
Rather than the business owner owning the system?
Yeah, yeah, exactly.
Yeah, yeah, everybody wants them.
We sold one in, in Los Angeles in about three months we put it on the market and within 24 hours we had 45 signed NDAs.
We had five offers on the table within a few weeks.
It was, it was really, really quick.
So, so yeah, super popular.
That's probably the space to look, so knowing that as well, Shep, I'll stick you on our mailing list.
But also, if I.
If I see any lead gen agencies come up for sale in the uk, I'll send you a link.
Yeah, absolutely.
Yeah.
Thank you.
Thank you so much.
No worries.
All right, look, good to meet you finally.
And, yeah, looking forward to working with you.
I'll get all of that stuff sent over.
All right.
Thank you so much.
All right, have a great day.
Have a great day.
Thank you.
Bye.
Bye.

summary.overview:
- Shep Ncube's Springboard Properties, generating 6,000 leads monthly, reported £5 million EBITDA last year, showcasing profitability and growth potential.  
- Shep plans to sell Springboard Properties by October to secure family finances; targeting a marketing agency acquisition for future growth.  
- Currently engaged with KBS for property sale but uncertain about their suitability as a broker, highlighting need for strategizing exit.  
- Shep aims for January readiness to acquire an agency, preferring larger firms (£5 million valuation) with established management structures for stability.  
- AI integration is a priority for Shep's future agency, emphasizing the need to adapt to technological advancements for client retention.  
- The US market offers attractive acquisition multiples (single to double digits) compared to lower UK multiples, influencing Shep's market preference.  
- Standard acquisition deal structure suggested is 50% cash upfront with 50% earnout over three years, ensuring transition involvement of founders.  
- Lead generation agencies identified as particularly valuable with high demand, evidenced by a recent LA agency's 45 signed NDAs within 24 hours.  
- Capital A's buy-side service model includes a £4,000 monthly retainer plus a 1.5% fee on successful acquisitions, outlining costs involved in agency purchases.  
- SBA loans of up to £5 million for US businesses offer funding opportunities for Shep, fitting well with his acquisition strategy and growth plans.
summary.short_summary: Shep Ncube, based in the Isle of Man, discussed his property marketing business, Springboard Properties, which generates 6,000 leads monthly and has a £5 million EBITDA. He plans to sell the company to secure family finances and then acquire a marketing agency to facilitate future acquisitions. Currently preparing for market launch, Shep aims for a January acquisition of a larger agency with a £5 million valuation, prioritizing AI services. Andy Day from Capital A clarified the M&A model, highlighting the differences in market multiples between the US and UK, and discussed a standard deal structure involving cash and earnout components. Insights on agency acquisition strategies and lead generation trends were also shared, emphasizing the value of stable agencies in both regions.
